claim.why_it_matters: The indented sub-entry 'Definition 22' is merged onto its parent's line, losing the index hierarchy and making 22 read as another page locator. Index only.

verdict.reasoning: Rendered PDF page 950 (printed page 926, index letter U, left column) shows 'UCS  10, 11, 22, 68, 85, 105, 532, 814, 824' on one line, then 'Definition  22' indented on the next line as a sub-entry. page-950.md line 37 reads 'UCS 10, 11, 22, 68, 85, 105, 532, 814, 824 Definition 22' on one line, with no line break and no   indent. The neighbouring entries keep both: 'UCS-4 phrase\' is followed by ' SPECIAL-NAMES paragraph 232'. So the sub-entry is merged into its parent's locator list, and the index hierarchy is lost. The claim quotes both sources correctly. The defect is in the index only and has no normative effect, so the structural severity is right.
